clue.text: Body of water in East Anglia, I hesitate to say, could be clearer

parts.words: Body of water in East Anglia
parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are shallow lakes in East Anglia; one of them is a broad
er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly describing a Norfolk lake as not quite clear enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Broads are a network of lakes and rivers in Norfolk and Suffolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broader explanation or hint is a plainer, more obvious one, so it is clearer than a narrow one.

clue.text: Almost get angry touring round English city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened verb surrounds the ring shape
almost tells us to drop the final letter of the word for getting angry

parts.note: to bristle is to show anger or indignation
a round thing, a ring, is the letter O

explanation.surface: A traveller nearly losing their temper while going round an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large port city in the south-west of England.

clue.text: Elated, as Hillary once was?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edmund Hillary stood on the summit of Everest in 1953, literally at the highest point on Earth

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's triumphant mood on the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for feeling elated pictures someone standing at the very top of the globe.

clue.text: In which rail fare may be taken?

definitions.text: In which rail fare may be taken?

parts.words: In which rail fare may be taken?
parts.note: fare here means food, not a ticket price; the carriage of a train where meals are eaten

explanation.surface: A question about where a train ticket is paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' tempts you towards ticket offices; it is food, as in 'bill of fare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage set aside for serving meals to passengers is where food is eaten on the train.

clue.text: Go over, touching ceiling

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
a cap is an upper limit, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: Reviewing something that concerns a spending ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise again or review what has been said is a short form of recapitulate.

clue.text: Powerful bishop and pawn on row

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A chess scene: a strong bishop with a pawn on the same rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes 'row' look like a line of squares; it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope, Bishop of Rome, is the most powerful bishop of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Soldier on exercises runs hard

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
severe means harsh or hard

explanation.surface: A soldier whose training runs are tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun; 'soldier on' is the verb phrase defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is the idiomatic sense of carrying on stubbornly.

clue.text: Relative, kind to conserve energy

indicators.note: conserving something means holding it in, so the word for kind keeps the energy symbol inside

parts.note: nice means kind or pleasant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A relative being kind enough to save energy at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Before anything else, leading article must be suppressed

indicators.note: suppressed means pressed down under, so the article is pushed into the phrase for leading

parts.note: someone leading a race is in first place
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An editor ruling that the newspaper's lead story must be spiked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' reads as a newspaper editorial; split it, 'leading' giving the phrase and 'article' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means firstly or to begin with, introducing the primary point.

clue.text: Sloshed, I initially fell over in opera

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the whole sequence is read from the bottom

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word fell

explanation.surface: A drunk confessing they fell down at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses OILED + I + F, giving FI-DELIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's only opera, about a wife who rescues her imprisoned husband.

clue.text: Credit card with notes lost — my mistake

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who lost a credit card and banknotes admits it was their fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges CREDITCARDNOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an admission of error, an acknowledgement that one was wrong.

clue.text: Simple goal — mine at home

parts.note: to tap a resource is to draw on it, to mine it
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: A footballer boasting that their easy goal came in a home game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive; it is the verb meaning exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a shot from very close range that needs only a gentle touch to score.

clue.text: Sample tea, perhaps, a little at a time

parts.note: a piece is a portion or specimen, a sample
tea is an example of a meal, the early evening one

explanation.surface: Tasting tea gradually, a sip at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can mean an evening meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Done gradually, piece by piece rather than all together.

clue.text: Provided during the French Revolution? How long a thing lasts!

indicators.note: during means within, so the conditional word sits inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
if means provided that
a cycle is one revolution, a full turn

explanation.surface: A question about the French Revolution and how long it lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The historical event is a red herring: the phrase must be broken apart, with 'during' placing the condition inside the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The series of stages a thing passes through from birth to death spans its whole existence.

clue.text: School subject in his term out in the outskirts of Coventry

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the outer letters of the city
the outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Coventry
out means not in proper order, so the letters of his term are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil studying a subject during a term away on the edge of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is only a link; 'out' signals the anagram, and the second 'in' places the shuffled letters between the city's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of substances and their reactions is taught in schools.

clue.text: Strain within small company to get capital

indicators.note: within puts the tune inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: Co is the short form of company
an air is a tune, a musical strain

explanation.surface: A strained small firm trying to raise capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like stress and 'capital' like money; they are a tune and a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Egypt, on the Nile.

clue.text: Mo changes exotic Chinese dress

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take an unusual new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Mo changing into an exotic Chinese dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'exotic' rearranges MOCHANGES.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting Chinese garment with a high collar and slit skirt, also called a qipao.

clue.text: Composer thrown out of Yale? Harvard

indicators.note: the composer's name comes out of the two university names, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A composer expelled from Yale and then Harvard.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Fortune endlessly provided, put on the Queen and deuce

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word for fortune

parts.note: luck is fortune
if means provided that
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A gambler's fortune falling short, the queen and a two dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deuce' looks like a card; it is an old word for the devil, as in 'what the deuce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan, and the deuce is an old euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: Cricket team's beginning to enjoy second drinks break

parts.note: a cricket team is an eleven; the possessive adds an S

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of enjoy

explanation.surface: A cricket team settling in to enjoy a second drinks interval.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket side has eleven players; ELEVENSES is a British mid-morning snack break.
explanation.definitionFit: A light mid-morning refreshment, tea or coffee, taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Timidity of head following fling

indicators.note: following puts the headland word after the throwing word

parts.note: to shy is to throw or fling
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A shy person's worry after a brief romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests an affair; it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashfulness or lack of confidence is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dramatist confronts nits dismissing first character for lack of grit

parts.note: Noël Coward was an English playwright

indicators.note: dismissing the first character means removing the opening letter of the word for the insects

parts.note: lice are the insects whose eggs are nits

explanation.surface: A playwright facing head lice and lacking the nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward wrote Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage, so a lack of it is fearfulness.

clue.text: Sovereign measure

definitions.meaning: a straight-edged instrument for measuring length

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch governs a realm, and a graduated straightedge measures length; both share the name.

clue.text: Awards for TV programmes, some of them mystifying

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Television awards whose choices baffle viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual American prizes honouring excellence in television.

clue.text: Snappy, one parking, after pressure is applied, in New York

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the abbreviation for the city
after puts the pressure symbol following the one-and-parking pair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A tetchy New Yorker after being pressured over parking.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy can mean sharp or curt, a snappish remark; it also means quick.

clue.text: Leave carrying early newspaper celebrating the past

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the word for leave contains the old paper

parts.note: to forsake is to abandon or leave
old means early, of former times
The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone leaving with an old newspaper as a keepsake of bygone days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' splits the verb for leave around its cargo; 'early' is an adjective for bygone, not a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something out of nostalgia, in memory of shared former days.

clue.text: Twentieth-century force ready, prepared to engage Royal Marines

indicators.note: to engage means to take in, so the rearranged letters enclose the marines
prepared means made up afresh, so the letters of ready are reworked

explanation.surface: A military force ready to fight the Royal Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like part of the surface's readiness for battle, but 'prepared' makes it anagram fodder, and 'to engage' takes the marines inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The army of the Soviet Union, founded after the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Politician interrupting rises nervously, smiles coyly

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the politician goes inside the rearranged word
nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters of rises are jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician interrupts, rises nervously and gives a coy smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reads as standing up, but 'nervously' marks it as anagram fodder that the politician breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to smile in an affected, silly or coquettish way.
